specs.text: All information created, transmitted, or stored on MTM technology assets is and remains the property of MTM.
Users must only use technology assets that are either approved by OCMS or are used in full compliance with MTM’s Mobile & BYOD Standard(A10487).
Users must not access MTM technology assets outside of Australia without approval.

MTM technology assets must not be used for illegal purposes, such as copyright infringement, obscenity, libel, slander, fraud, defamation, plagiarism, harassment, intimidation, forgery, impersonation, illegal gambling, soliciting for illegal pyramid schemes, or any form of computer tampering.
Users must respect copyright, trademarks, and intellectual property laws in all activities involving MTM technology assets.
Users must not interfere, tamper, damage or bypass user authentication or security mechanisms of any MTM technology assets.
Users must not introduce unapproved software into MTM technology assets unless it’s approved by OCMS.
MTM technology assets must be secured at all times, including locking devices when unattended and physically securing them when not in use.
Users must not monitor, record, scan or sweep network traffic unless authorised by Security Operations or Cybersecurity Team.
User must not use consumer-based VPN services (e.g., VPNExpress, NordVPN, SurfShark etc) while accessing MTM technology asset.
Users must not connect any unapproved devices, such as devices that are capable of bridging connections, providing wireless connectivity, altering network topology, or enabling remote access.
Users must only connect BYOD devices to designated guest networks in accordance with the Mobile Device & BYOD Security Standard (A10487).

Users must not disclose account credentials to anyone else or allow another person to use their account. Impersonating, password guessing or logging in using another users’ credentials is also prohibited.
User must assess the sensitivity of information and handle it according to the MTM Information Classification Standard (A9447) and Information Asset Secure Handling Guideline (A9443).

MTM information must only be stored in approved storage locations (e.g., corporate network drives, MTM Microsoft SharePoint, MTM Microsoft OneDrive, MTM Microsoft Teams, and approved internal applications and databases).
Users must not access, copy, or modify any corporate MTM data/information without strict prior authorisation from the respective information/asset owners.
Users must not use personal removable media. All removable media use must adhere to Removable media standard (A10382).
Sensitive conversations must be conducted in person.
Users must maintain awareness of the environment and ensure confidential or sensitive data is not viewed or communicated in public locations.
Users must refer to the New Emerging and Advancing Technology Security Guideline (A12293) before using technologies like AI, robotics, or augmented reality.
Users must comply to all MTM policies and standards relevant to their role and responsibilities.
Users must inform their manager and/or OCMS when system access is no longer required.
Users must report any theft, loss, damage, or suspected security incident involving MTM assets to the OCMS Technology Service Desk.

evidence: Acceptable use policy acknowledgement records for users of the system
Security awareness training completion records
List of approved devices and technology used to access the system

Reasonable personal use of MTM computers, internet and email is permissible if it does not: a. Interfere with productivity. b. Interfere with any other employees. c. Interfere with any business activities. d. Compromise the security of technology assets. e. Breach any MTM policies and standards. f. Violate laws, regulations, or orders. g. Consume MTM Helpdesk and/or IT resources. MTM accepts no liability for any personal loss or damages suffered by users because of personal use.
Personal reasonable use of MTM technology assets for non-work-related activities must comply with MTM's policies and standards.

MTM technology assets must not be used for personal activities that degrade system performance or consume excessive network bandwidth, such as cryptocurrency mining or outsourcing processing power to third parties
Users must protect MTM technology assets from damage, theft, or unauthorized access at all times.

Acceptable use acknowledgement records

specs.text: Users must exercise caution with emails from unknown senders, and report suspicious messages using the phishing button in Microsoft Outlook.
Users must adhere to Metro social media Policy (A7630) which outlines the use of social media in the workplace and provides guidelines for acceptable use for all Metro employees.

Users must not attempt to access areas of the internet, through MTM network, containing content relating to Dark/Deep Web, hacking, viruses, malware, scams, or Peer-to-Peer file sharing, unless authorised.
Users must not engage in cyberbullying, harassment, or any form of intimidation through MTM technology assets.
Users must not send or forward unsolicited or junk email including advertising, jokes, chain letters and pyramid schemes.
User must not automatically forward MTM emails, files, or other information to external destinations, including but not limited to personal mailboxes, is strictly prohibited.
User must not comment or post work-related activities, images and videos on social media websites unless otherwise authorised as per social media policy[A7630].
MTM data must not be transferred outside of MTM-owned systems, such as via unapproved USB drives or external cloud storage, unless explicitly authorized.

Authorized MTM personnel may monitor and log user activities on MTM networks for security, audit, or maintenance purposes.
Line managers in conjunction with cyber security and people services could limit an employee’s personal use of MTM technology assets; if deemed necessary.

specs.text: Implement controls that prevent or detect malicious code in software & website. (ISO/IEC)
Implement controls to detect, eradicate and repair system with malicious code (ISO)
Anti-Malware protection is implemented on network gateway to detect and eradicate malicious code from untrusted network.
Anti-Malware must be able to analyse the characteristics and behaviour of malicious code. (NIST)
The anti-malware software has a signature-based or heuristic-based detection enabled. (ISM)
Anti-Malware software must automatically scan for malware of any files received over networks, via email or via any form of storage medium (fixed disk, DVDs, CDs, USB, memory cards etc). (ISO/NIST)
The anti-malware software must have reputation rating and ransomware protection functionality enabled. (ISM)

Malware detection mechanism to be able to detect integrity violations of application binaries and data files; (IEC) Techniques may include, but are not limited to, binary integrity and attributes monitoring, hashing and signature techniques. Mitigation techniques may include, but are not limited to, file cleaning, quarantining, file deletion, host communication restriction and IPSs. (IEC)
There is a central management and reporting for malicious code protection. The control system must provide the capability to manage malicious code protection mechanisms. (IEC)

Virus definition files must be kept up to date at least on a daily basis; (ISO/ISM) Note: Exception to the clause is permissible if device is not connected to any network (air-gapped). Virus definition can be updated during maintenance scheduled for the devices.
Anti-Malware software must be active, be scheduled to perform malicious code system scan at least on a weekly basis; (ISO)
Update malicious code protection mechanisms/software when current version is no longer supported.
Update malicious code protection mechanisms/software as new releases are available. (NIST)
Activities for the activation and de-activation of anti-malware must be logged & monitored. (ISO)
Anti-malware alerts must be logged and monitored through a central Security information and event management (SIEM) solution.
Incorporate the results from malicious code detection and analysis into organisational incident response and remediation processes. (ISO/NIST)

evidence: Anti-malware / EDR console report showing coverage for all system hosts
Signature or engine update status report
Scan schedule and recent scan results
Sample malware alert showing it reaches the SOC / SIEM

specs.text: There must be a documented software development process to ensure the implementation of security in application. Roles and responsibility for the implementation of security on application must be identified. The document must be consistent with applicable laws, privacy requirement and aligned with organisational objective. (ISO, NIST, IEC, MTM)

Application development must follow the principle of secure by design. “Secure-by-Design” means that technology products are built in a way that reasonably protects against malicious cyber actors successfully gaining access to devices, data, and connected infrastructure. (ISO, ISM, NIST, IEC, MTM)

Cyber Security must be consulted throughout the development life cycle of an application. This will ensure consistency with the organisation-wide secure design principles and risk management. (ISO, NIST, IEC, MTM)
All development activities must be carried out only by authorised personnel (MTM employee and MTM contracted vendors). (MTM)
All developers must keep up to date to relevant security policies, standards, and training. (MTM)

MTM’s Change Management process must be followed for any new or iterative deployments. All security controls and functionality must be validated and documented prior to the deployment or changes made to the application. (NIST/MTM)
All application security-related issues must be treated prior to the deployment or changes made to the application. (ISO, NIST, ISM, IEC, MTM)

For any new or iterative deployment of product, product documentation must be updated with following content (IEC): a) Updated product descriptions & security features, b) Updated maintenance & Support instructions, and c) Updated Configuration baseline settings.

evidence: Documented secure development lifecycle or procedure
Change records showing security review and approval
Secure coding standard or developer training records

specs.text: Development Environment must be segregated from production environment. Development and modification of software only takes place in development environments. (ISO, ISM, IEC, MTM)
All changes impacting security must be tested and verified before implementation in a production environment. (ISO, NIST, IEC, MTM)

Confidential (official-sensitive) or restricted (protected) Data from production environments must not be used in a development or testing environment unless the environment is secured to the same level as the production environment (MTM).
Development and testing environments must not use the same data source/repositories as the production environments. (ISM, IEC, MTM)
All other non-production environment (such as Test, UAT and Pre-production) should be segregated from production environment.?

specs.text: Application must be deployed on an authorized system. (NIST/MTM)

Secure header configuration must be implemented for web applications. Controls for security header configuration are as follows (ISM, IEC, MTM): a) Security headers are properly set on the application. b) Implement Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options in response headers. c) Header output is URL encoded.

User Input Validation or sanitisation must be performed on all input handled by applications or assurance to be provided in case of COTS application. Controls for input validation are as follows (ISO, ISM, NIST, IEC, MTM): a) User input is validated for type, length, format, and range. b) Validation on user input must be performed on server side. c) Uploaded files must be validated for content type, size, file type and filename. d) Uploaded files must be scanned for malicious content. e) Special characters are sanitized before being used in systems. f) All page output is properly encoded.
Security controls to avoid bypassing authentication and authorization must be implemented. Authentication and Authorization checks must be performed on each access request. (MTM)
Verification must be done to ensure that all incorporated libraries do not possess high-risk vulnerabilities. (MTM)
All libraries must be up to date with latest security patches. (MTM)

The application must identify and address error conditions to facilitate effective remediation. Error messages must not disclose information that could be exploited by adversaries, unless revealing such information is necessary for timely troubleshooting. (ISO, NIST, IEC, MTM)

Secure configuration for application session management must be implemented for web application as follows (ISO, NIST, ISM, MTM): a) Session tokens must not be passed in URLs. b) Session timeout must be configured to 4 hours (idle) or less. c) Encrypt session data. d) Logout must result in the invalidation of the session.

Application configuration must be securely implemented as follows (excludes COTS application) (MTM): a) It must be ensured that sensitive information, such as username/password, is not hardcoded in source code or application. b) The application must undergo a peer review to ensure that it is free from backdoors. c) There is a fail-safe method within the application, ensuring that in the event of unexpected failures or errors, the system can gracefully handle and prevent data loss or service disruption.

Sensitive and confidential data including PII data requires the following controls to be implemented (ISM, IEC, MTM): a) All sensitive data must be removed/obfuscated/masked by default. b) Sensitive information is only revealed to authorised users. c) Sensitive information is not logged.
The database server and application server must be functionally and logically separated. (ISM, IEC, MTM)
All queries made from applications to databases must be verified to ensure legitimate content and correctness of syntax (ISM, IEC).

Capacity planning must be performed to guarantee adequate resources for application processing, communication, and storage. Configure system/application thresholds to restrict resource consumption and optimize the efficient management of resources/memory. (NIST/MTM)
Backup and recovery process must be available for the application. The process must be able to recover and reconstitute to a known secure state after a disruption or failure. (NIST/IEC)

All internet-facing applications must be protected by a Web Application Firewall (WAF). The WAF must be configured with customized security policies to address the unique requirements and vulnerabilities of each application, ensuring comprehensive protection against potential threats and vulnerabilities.
Application security logging must be implemented as per MTM Security Event Logging and Monitoring standard. (ISO, NIST, IEC)

Mechanism should be implemented to verify the integrity of both data and application components throughout their lifecycle. This can include the implementation of checksum for the application binaries. (NIST, ISM)
Automated tools should be leveraged for static and dynamic code review. (MTM)

All new application, including any major changes made on an application, should be tested for vulnerabilities before being deployed.
All application security should be tested and validated by manual code review or by static application security testing (SAST). (ISO, NIST, IEC, ISM)
Peer review is performed throughout the software development life cycle. (NIST, ISM)

Application security can be tested and validated by performing threat and vulnerability analysis, sandboxing, application penetration testing and dynamic application security testing (DAST). (ISO, NIST, IEC, ISM)

specs.text: All databases must have identified owners assigned to them, ensuring clear accountability for the data stored within. (ISO, NIST, MTM)
File-based access controls are applied to database files. (ISM, IEC)
MTM must implement database encryption for data classified as Confidential (official-sensitive) or restricted (protected).
Database servers must be placed on a different network segment to user workstations. (ISM)
The need-to-know principle is enforced for database contents through restricting minimum privileges, utilizing database views, and implementing database roles. (ISM, IEC)
Parameterised queries or stored procedures are used for database interaction instead of dynamically generated queries. (ISM, IEC)

specs.text: All public facing Application Programming Interface (API) must implement authentication and authorization mechanism. This should comply with MTM Identity and Access Management Standard (A10102). API Key should only be used for API client authentication and authorization mechanism. Check if the logged-in user has access to perform requested actions. (OWASP)

All public facing APIs must be protected from Server-Side request forgery using following methods: (OWASP) a) Use allow list for remote origins. b) URL schemes, ports, and media types. c) Disable HTTP redirections. d) Utilize a reliable URL parser to prevent parsing inconsistencies. e) Validate and sanitize all client input data and avoid sending raw responses to clients.
All API must have a designated owner, ensuring clear accountability and responsibility for the security of the API (OWASP, MTM)

All API must ensure restrictive resource consumption to avoid resource starvation. Following controls must be implemented: (OWASP) a) Limit resource utilization (e.g., memory, Number of restarts, processes, and spending) based on the requirement. b) Enforce maximum data sizes for inputs and payload. c) Implement rate limiting and frequency limits.
Restrict and limit the access to sensitive API. (OWASP)
All API must be securely hardened. (OWASP)
Always validate data received and transmitted to third party APIs before using it (OWASP)

specs.text: Cybersecurity risk management practices must adhere to MTM's Integrated Risk Management Procedure (A2023). This ensures a structured and consistent approach to risk management. (MTM)

Cybersecurity Threat Risk Assessment (TRA) must be conducted for all new applications or systems introduced into the environment and for any changes that impact data flow, data classification or system/network architecture in existing systems. (MTM)

Risk identification can occur through assessments, audits, incidents, or concerns raised internally. Each identified cybersecurity risk must be assigned to a responsible risk owner. The risk owner is accountable for managing, reviewing, and addressing the risk with appropriate oversight. (MTM)

MTM must conduct a Maturity Assessment every two years to review organizational cybersecurity risks. The findings will be documented in the INX system and classified as enterprise cybersecurity risks. (MTM/FA-T)

The use of removable media on MTM-owned or operated systems is prohibited. However, in circumstances where removable media is the only viable solution for information storage and sharing, an exception to use removable media must be obtained.
It is required to use MTM-approved methods and solutions (e.g., MTM Secure File Transfer, Team, OneDrive, SharePoint etc.) to store and share information between systems and users.
A removable media exception can only be authorised if there is a business reason, and it is approved by the user’s manager and general manager of the business.
Removable media must have an identifiable owner.
Only MTM-provided removable media devices can be used. Users must not use non approved removable media devices.
Removal media must be scanned for malware before use.
Only authorised personnel are allowed to handle removable media and ensure accountability for transport outside of controlled areas.

Sensitive Data (classified as confidential/official-sensitive or restricted/protected) must not be stored in removable media. If these data are required to be stored in removable media, approval is required from the information owner.
Sensitive Data (classified as confidential/official-sensitive or restricted/protected) must be encrypted.
Loss of removable media with any data on it must be reported to security operations.
All media that is no longer in use or functional must return to Desktop Support. Media must be sanitised and disposed securely in accordance with MTM Processes

evidence: Entry for the system in the risk register with owner
Latest risk review minutes or report

specs.text: Cybersecurity risk assessments will adhere to AS/NZS ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management Standard (ISO-RM) and OVIC Practitioner Guide – Information Security Risk Management version 2.0 (ISRM).
Before conducting an assessment, the System-under-Consideration (SuC) must be defined, including boundaries and associated assets. (ISO-RM/ISRM)
Consult relevant subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify potential risks and assess their organizational impact. (ISO-RM/ISRM)

Risk identification must consider vulnerabilities and threats (hazards), their potential impact on affected assets, and the duration of these impacts. (MTM, ISO RM /ISRM) Note: Duration is important when there is a loss of availability. A longer duration can increase the severity of the impact. For example, losing a Train Control System for 10 minutes, 4 hours, or 1 day will result in increasingly severe operational disruptions.

A Business Impact Level (BIL) Assessment must be conducted to identify and assess the potential business impact of a cybersecurity breach on the affected asset. The BIL Assessment will evaluate key risk drivers, including the impact on Confidentiality, Integrity, or Availability (CIA). This assessment provides critical insight into the severity of the potential consequences of a breach and helps prioritize risk mitigation efforts. (MTM/NIST/ISO)
The MITRE ATT&CK framework is recommended for threat identification to ensure comprehensive coverage of adversarial tactics, techniques, and procedures. (MTM)

As part of completing the Business Impact Level (BIL) Assessment form (A10057), a severity impact value must be assigned to quantify the potential consequences on a system in the event of a cybersecurity incident. This impact value should reflect the potential effect on the system’s Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA). The assigned severity value will guide risk prioritization and inform subsequent mitigation strategies. (MTM)

The likelihood of a risk materializing must be determined by evaluating the effectiveness of existing controls in accordance with MTM Cybersecurity Standards. This assessment should consider historical occurrences of similar risks and account for future factors, such as the intent, motivation, and capability of human adversaries or other threat actors. This comprehensive evaluation will support a more accurate and dynamic risk profile. (ISRM)

Risk determination and rating must follow the MTM Integrated Risk Procedure. A risk ratings matrix (found in MTM Integrated Risk Procedure) will be used to assess risks by combining the severity impact (as determined in RC.2.7) and the likelihood of occurrence (as evaluated in RC.2.8). This matrix will provide a structured approach to categorizing risks and enable the prioritization of remediation actions based on both impact and likelihood. (MTM)

All identified risks must undergo evaluation to determine those that require immediate prioritization for mitigation. Risks with the highest ratings, based on their impact and likelihood, must be addressed first to minimize risk to the organization. (ISRM)

The outcome of the risk treatment must result in one of the following actions (MTM): a) No remediation required - The assessment determines that the system can proceed without any further remediation action. b) Remediate identified risk before system use - Any identified risks must be remediated before the system is in operation. c) Risk management if risk is not mitigated - If the risk cannot be remediated prior to system use, the following steps must be taken: i. MTM risk process must be followed to manage the risk. ii. If there are any exceptions against MTM cybersecurity standards, the exceptions must be recorded in the Cyber Exception Register.
All removable media must be tracked and registered.
The usage of removable media should be monitored.
The following security controls should be available for removable media: (ISM/MTM) a) Write block capability, b) Encryption capability, and c) Password Protection.
If no longer required, the contents of any removable media should be removed and unrecoverable.
Processes or Procedures must be developed and implemented for media destruction and disposal.
MTM data must be securely removed from associated media, prior to off-site maintenance, disposal, or re-use.
Authorisation is required for media that is removed from the organisation and a record of such removals must be maintained to ensure an audit trail.
The destruction of media must be performed under the supervision of at least one person, ensuring and endorsing that the destruction is successfully completed.
All media destruction, sanitization and disposal must be approved, tracked, and documented.
Prior to media disposal, labels and markings indicating the owner, sensitivity, classification, or any other marking that can associate the media with its prior use must be removed.

evidence: Completed TRA / risk assessment report with scope and BIL
Risk treatment plan with owners and dates

specs.text: MTM must not act or engage in any practice that, contravenes the Victorian Protective Data Security Standards (VPDSS) nor omit anything that is required by the standard. (FA-T)

For Cybersecurity, MTM has contractual obligations under the Franchise Agreement to comply with (FA-T): a) AS/NZS ISO 31000:2009 Risk Management Standard. b) AS/NZS ISO/IEC 27005:2012 Information technology – Security techniques - Information security risk management. c) Promptly notify DTP upon becoming aware of any non-compliance with any standard listed above (reference to (a) & (b)), together with details of the response or action which the Franchisee will take to remedy the non compliance; and d) Promptly notify DTP once a non-compliance has been remedied.

MTM must implement security measures to protect Personal Information and MTM important records from misuse, interference, loss, unauthorized access, modification, or disclosure, in accordance with the MTM Privacy Policy. (FA-T)

MTM must ensure appropriate levels of security exist to ensure resistance from internal or external intrusion or attacks and ensure this level is maintained by regularly undertaking independent assessment of security risks. MTM must adopt appropriate business and operational control systems, security policies and standards consistent with the appropriate legislative requirements. (FA-O)

MTM must develop or update a Protective Data Security Plan (PDSP) once every 2 years. PDSP contain tactical and strategic plan that address the security risks identified in the SRPA. PDSP must be adequately address all relevant security considerations from VPDSS and ISO/IEC 27001:2013 (FA-T).
PDSP must be approved by DTP and executed by MTM. It is required that MTM update the PDSP when there is any significant change in the operating environment, or security risks. (FA-T)
A maturity assessment against the VPDSS must be performed once every two years, alternating with the PDSP submission date. (FA-T)
As part of BAU, update on SRPA and PDSP will be provided in monthly DTP SMO meeting. (FA-T)

In an event of data breach, MTM must notify DTP in writing within one hour of becoming aware of the Data Security Breach. MTM must take all necessary steps to promptly remedy the Data Security Breach and reinstate any affected Data Systems or Data. MTM is required to comply with direction issued by DTP. (FA-T)

OCMS works, including inspection task or routine maintenance task, must include any checks required in the Protective Data Security Plan in which case the reporting shall be against the timeframes stipulated in the Protective Data Security Plan. (FT-O)

Maturity assessment evidence
Incident or breach notification procedure

specs.text: The approved asymmetric/public key algorithms are as follows (ISM): a) Diffie-Hellman (DH) for agreeing on encryption session keys b) Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) for digital signatures c) Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) for key exchange d) Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) for digital signatures e) Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) for digital signatures and passing encryption session keys or similar keys. Note: ECDH and ECDSA should be used whenever possible
The only approved symmetric encryption algorithm is Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). When using AES for encryption, AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256 must be used, with a preference for AES-256. (ISM
The targets used to ensure the effective security strength of algorithms listed in this section must be at least 112 bits. (ISM)
For Diffie–Hellman (DH), a minimum of 2048 bits is required (this provides 112 bits of effective security strength). (ISM)

When using elliptic curve cryptography for session keys, a curve from FIPS 186-4 must be used. For ECDH, a base point order and key size of at least 224 bits are required, providing an effective security strength of 112 bits. Therefore, it is recommended to use NIST P-256, P-384, or P-521 curves, with a preference for the NIST P-384 curve. (ISM)

When using RSA for digital signatures and passing encryption session keys or similar keys, a modulus of at least 2048 bits is used, with a preference for 3072 bits, providing an effective security strength of 112 bits. (ISM)
The only approved hashing algorithm is Secure Hashing Algorithm 2 (SHA-2). When using SHA-2 for hashing, an output size of at least 224 bits is required, with a preference for SHA 384. (ISM)

The approved Cryptographic Protocols are as follows: a) Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 and above b) Secure Shell (SSH) version 2.0 c) Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension (S/MIME) version 2.0 d) OpenPGP Message Format e) Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) f) Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 g) Wi-Fi Protected Access 3.

Only TLS 1.2 and above must be used for TLS connections. TLS must be configured as follows: a) AES-GCM is used for encryption of TLS connections. b) Only server-initiated secure renegotiation is used for TLS connections. c) DH or ECDH is used for key establishment of TLS connections. d) When using DH or ECDH for key establishment of TLS connections, the ephemeral variant is used. e) Anonymous DH is not used for TLS connections. f) SHA-2-based certificates are used for TLS connections. g) SHA-2 is used for the Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) and pseudorandom function (PRF) for TLS connections. h) TLS compression is disabled for TLS connections. i) Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) is used for TLS connections.

SSH version 2 must be used. SSH must be configured as follows: a) Public key-based authentication is used for SSH connections. b) SSH private keys are protected with a passphrase or a key encryption key. c) SSH Daemon listen on the required interfaces (ListenAddress xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx) d) SSH Daemon has a suitable login banner (Banner x) e) SSH Daemon a login authentication timeout of no more than 60 seconds (LoginGraceTime 60) f) SSH Daemon disable host-based authentication (HostbasedAuthentication no) g) SSH Daemon disable rhosts-based authentication (IgnoreRhosts yes) h) SSH Daemon disable the ability to login directly as root (PermitRootLogin no) i) SSH Daemon disable empty passwords (PermitEmptyPasswords no) j) SSH Daemon disable connection forwarding (AllowTCPForwarding no) k) SSH Daemon disable gateway ports (GatewayPorts no) l) SSH Daemon disable X11 forwarding (X11Forwarding no).

IPsec can be operated in tunnel mode or transport mode. The tunnel mode of operation is preferred as it provides full encapsulation of IP packets while the transport mode of operation only encapsulates the payload of IP packets

IPsec connection be secured as follows: a) Use ESP protocol is used for authentication and encryption. b) Use IKE version for key exchange. c) AES is used for encrypting IPsec connections, preferably ENCR_AES_GCM_16. d) PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256, PRF_HMAC_SHA2_384 or PRF_HMAC_SHA2_512 is used for IPsec connections, preferably PRF_HMAC_SHA2_512. e) AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_384_192, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_512_256 or NONE (only with AES-GCM) is used for authenticating IPsec connections, preferably NONE. f) DH or ECDH is used for key establishment of IPsec connections, preferably 384-bit random ECP group, 3072-bit MODP Group or 4096-bit MODP Group. g) A security association lifetime of less than four hours (14400 seconds) is used for IPsec connections. h) PFS is used for IPsec connections

evidence: Cryptographic configuration showing approved algorithms and key lengths
Scan results showing weak protocols (for example TLS 1.0/1.1) are disabled

specs.text: A user provisioning and de-provisioning process shall be implemented to enable assignment of access rights. Access will only be granted when request has been validated and approved. (ISO, NIST, MTM, ISM)
Users shallonly be provided with access that they are authorized to use. No access to any resources or services will be granted without authorisation. (ISM, MTM, ISO)

Access controls shall be implemented based on the principles of least-privilege and need-to-know. Allowing only authorized accesses for users that are necessary to accomplish assigned organisational tasks. (VPDSS, NIST)

Based on the Segregation of Duties (SOD) principle, conflicting duties and areas of responsibility should be segregated to reduce opportunities for unauthorized or unintentional modification or misuse of the organisation’s assets. (ISO, MTM)
There is a unique identifier for each login session. Session timeout shall be configured to 4 hours (idle) or less (excluding service account). (NIST, MTM)
There shall be audit logging for the administration of account (e.g. creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions). (NIST)
There shall be audit logging for successful and failed login attempts. (MTM)

All accounts to systems and applications shall be disabled within 30 days when (ISO, ISM, MTM), a) Personnel Leave MTM, b) Personnel reached contract completion, c) Account no longer associated with a user or individual, d) Account is in violation of organisational policy, or e) Account is inactive for 90 days.
Account shall be deleted when an account is no longer required after 180 days. (MTM)

Asset owners shall revalidate and review users access rights at least once a year. This includes the review of privileges assigned and to validate the need for such privileges; and reassign or remove privileges, if necessary, to correctly reflect organisational mission and business needs. (ISO, MTM)

specs.text: Request for privileged user access to systems, applications and data repositories will only be granted when request has been authorised. (ISM)

Restrict privileged user accounts on the system to authorised personnel in accordance with the Least Privilege principle. (ISO/NIST) a) Privileged user access shall be restricted to users who have a valid operational requirement and are unable to perform the job function with a standard user account. b) Privileged users are assigned a dedicated privileged account to be used solely for tasks requiring privileged access. c) Privileged users shall only use a standard user account, and not privilege user account, for regular day-to-day business use.

Privileged users should use separate privileged and unprivileged operating environments. Using different physical workstations is the most secure approach to separating privileged and unprivileged operating environments for system administrators. However, a virtualisation-based solution may be sufficient for separating privileged and unprivileged operating environments. (ISM, MTM, VPDSS)
The privilege user account shall be disabled or removed when it is no longer required. (ISM, MTM)

MTM authorised identity and access solution (e.g. Privilege Access Management) shall be used for privileged user account management. An inventory of all privileged user accounts to production systems shall be classified, protected and hosted. The inventory shall be updated to identify new or changed accounts. (MTM)

Privileged user access to MTM systems shall comply with the following: a) Shall be centrally managed through MTM authorised identity and access solution, b) Password rotated in accordance with MTM password requirement, c) Logged and record all activities performed by Administrator, and d) Logout immediately once tasks have been completed.
Privilege access should be authenticated using multi-factor authentication.

Usage of Privileged user accounts shall comply with the following (MTM): a) Shall never have an associated mailbox, b) Shall never have access to email, c) Shall never be used for running scheduled tasks (consider service accounts), and d) Shall never be shared.
Local administrator privileges shall not be granted to MTM Standard user accounts. (MTM)
All privileged access and activities shall be logged and periodically reviewed to detect unauthorized or inappropriate use. (MTM)

specs.text: MTM should employ automated tools for strong password generation (NIST)

Passwords are not based on words found in a dictionary, including foreign language, or exist in a language as slang, dialect, or jargon. Passwords are not a list of categorised words; do not form a real sentence in a natural language; and are not constructed from song lyrics, movies, literature or any other publicly available material. (MTM/ISM)
Passwords for separate systems shall be unique, unpredictable, and not reused. (MTM, ISM)

All MTM user account passwords a. Minimum Password Length: 12 characters (No Null Password) b. Password Complexity required and shall contain characters from three of the following four categories: Uppercase alphabetic characters (A-Z), Lowercase alphabetic characters (a-z), Numerical characters (0-9), Special characters: ~!@#$%^&*_-+=`|\(){}[]:;"'<>,.?/ c. Password History: 8 passwords remembered d. Minimum Password Age: 0 e. Maximum Password Age: 365 days f. Password Never Expires: Not Permitted g. Account Lockout Threshold: 3 invalid attempts h. Account Lockout Duration: 30 minutes i. Reset Account Lockout Counter After: 30 minutes Administrator and Privilege User Account Password control is the same as MTM User Account, except for the following: a. Minimum Password Length: 20 b. Maximum Password Age: 30 days (MTM, CyberArk)
Service Account password, Emergency Account password and Key Management password shall be at least 20 characters long.
Credentials provided to users shall be changed on first use. (ISM)
Password shall be stored in a format that cannot be reversed. An example is storing the password using a salted keyed hash. (NIST, ISM, MTM)
Passwords shall be transmitted over encrypted channels (cryptographically protected). (NIST)
Require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery or reset (NIST, MTM)

Passwords are required to be changed if (MTM): a) They are directly compromised, b) They are suspected of being compromised, c) They appear in an online data breach database, d) They are discovered stored on networks in the clear, or e) They are discovered being transferred across networks in the clear. f) Using of weak password is detected. Note: User will be contacted by MTM OCMS and forced to change their password within 14 days of detection if any of the above are detected by security operations.
The display and printing of passwords shall be masked, suppressed, or otherwise obscured so that unauthorised parties will not be able to observe or subsequently recover them. (CyberArk)

specs.text: All MTM-managed Mobile Devices, such as smartphones, tablets, and laptops, must be enrolled and centrally managed by a Mobile Device Management solution. The following minimum-security controls must be implemented for MTM-managed Mobile Devices: a) Devices must have the MTM-approved standard operational environment (SOE) installed and configured. b) MTM security controls must be in place to protect the devices from external threats and malware. c) Security updates should be regularly updated in accordance with MTM patch cadence. d) Devices must be protected with password authentication as per the MTM Standard or with multifactor authentication.
MTM-managed Mobile Devices must prevent personnel from installing or uninstalling non approved applications.
MTM-managed Mobile Devices must prevent personnel from disabling or modifying security functionality once provisioned. (ISM)
Users and asset owners of MTM are accountable for any information that is stored or transmitted through MTM-managed Mobile Devices.
To prevent unauthorised access to MTM information, full storage encryption must be enabled on all MTM-managed Mobile Devices.

All MTM-managed mobile devices must be locked and protected by a PIN code (minimum 6 digits), password, or Face ID. The mobile device needs to be automatically locked after a maximum of 3 minutes of inactivity.
All MTM-managed Mobile Devices must be asset labelled with a MTM contact details. This is to ensure that lost and found devices can be returned to MTM.
Deregistration of MTM-managed Mobile Devices must erase all MTM information.
Jailbroken/Rooted mobile devices are not permitted to connect to, or access MTM information systems/assets.
Sideloading or transferring of files between two devices, in particular between a system and a mobile device, are not permitted in MTM.
All MTM-managed mobile devices should be configured to remain undiscoverable to other Bluetooth devices except during Bluetooth pairing.

Web content filtering should be applied to inbound web traffic (ISM): a) filter potentially harmful web-based content, b) block malicious, dynamic, and anonymously registered domain names, c) block files identified as malicious, or those that cannot be inspected, and d) block attempts to access websites through IP addresses instead domain names.

Security mechanisms, service levels and management requirements of all network services must be identified and included in network services agreements, whether these services are provided in-house or outsourced. (ISO27002)
Only privileged administrators are allowed to enable and disable security configurations and policy. (NIST/MTM/ISM)
Unused services and ports on network devices must be disabled. (NIST/MTM)
Network must be configured to prevent incomplete transmission, misrouting, unauthorised message alteration, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised message duplication or replay. (ISO27002)
All Network Management traffic must be encrypted. (MTM)
Where addresses are allocated dynamically, standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and the lease duration must be assigned to devices (NIST)
Terminate the network connection at the end of communication session [NIST/MTM].
Use Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) version 3 on networks, ensuring that data packets are authenticated and encrypted over the network. (ISO27002/NIST/MTM/ISM)
There is a standard operating environments (SOEs) for all network assets. (VPDSS/MTM)
All security events for network devices must be logged and monitored. (MTM)

specs.text: Network access controls must prevent the connection of unauthorised network devices and limit network traffic to only those required for business purpose. (ISM/MTM/NIST)

Gateway controls must be designed to regulate data flows to (ISM/MTM): a) separate networks belonging to different security domains and untrusted network, b) only allow explicitly authorised data flows, and c) inspect and filter data flows at the transport and above network layers.
Network IDS or IPS must be used on gateways between MTM’s networks and any public or untrusted network. (ISM/MTM/NIST)
Firewall must be used to ensure separation between MTM’s networks and any public or untrusted network. (ISM/MTM/NIST)
Firewall must be designed with the following filtering rules (ISM/IEC62443/MTM): a) deny network traffic by default, and b) deny access requests via untrusted networks unless explicitly approved.
Information transmitted between MTM’s networks, and any public or untrusted network must be encrypted. (MTM)
A demilitarised zone is required for any external access to MTM’s services.

Denial-of-Service & Distributed Denial-of-Service prevention must be established at network boundary (IEC62443/MTM): a) capability to restrict the ability to cause DoS/DDoS events b) be equipped to provide the capability to manage communication loads (such as using rate limiting) to mitigate the effects of information and/or message flooding types of DoS/DDoS events, and provide the capability to operate in a degraded mode during a DoS/DDoS event.

Web content filtering must be applied to outbound web traffic to (ISM): a) filter potentially harmful web-based content, b) block malicious, dynamic, and anonymously registered domain names, c) block files identified as malicious, or those that cannot be inspected, and block attempts to access websites through IP addresses instead domain names.
All web access must be logged using web proxies, including that by internal servers, and must be protected from unauthorised access and modification. (ISO27002/NIST/MTM/ISM)
Authenticated proxy servers are required to route all internal communications traffic to external networks. (ISM/MTM/NIST)
IPv6 tunnelling must be blocked by network security appliances at externally connected network boundaries. (ISM/MTM/NIST)

For MTM managed network and telecommunication infrastructure, alternate telecommunication services must be verified at least once a year. (NIST/VPDSS)

Primary and alternate telecommunications service agreements must be developed to contain priority-of-service provisions in accordance with MTM's availability requirements including recovery time objectives. (NIST/VPDSS)

The capability to prevent any communication through the control system boundary when there is an operational failure of the boundary protection mechanisms (also termed fail close) must be provided. (IEC62443/MTM)

All network LAN Switch must have duplicated (uplink) fibre interfaces to neighbouring or higher-level switches to prevent loss of communication in the event of any single uplink interface port or cable core failure. (MTM)
All routers must be fitted with redundant power supplies. (MTM)

All network equipment and infrastructure must be connected to an uninterruptible power source (UPS). The UPS battery capacity shall provide a minimum of 2 hours backup operation time for the network. (MTM)
Primary and alternate telecommunications service providers must be required to have contingency plans that are reviewed to ensure compliance with MTM's contingency requirements. (NIST)
Evidence of contingency testing by primary and alternate telecommunications service providers must be obtained at least once a year. (NIST)

The execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access is required to ensure activities are logged in a format that provides assessable evidence. (NIST)

specs.text: The following security events must be logged on all system or application (NIST/ISO/MTM): a) Action to Add/Delete/Modify Users Accounts b) Password changes c) Failed logons and account lockouts, d) Unauthorised or failed access, e) Successful user logons and logoffs, f) Changes to security attributes/policies and configurations, g) Administrative and privileged action or usage, and h) System crash and error messages

Ensure that security event records contain information that establishes the following (NIST): a) What type of event occurred; b) When the event occurred; c) Where the event occurred; d) Source of the event; e) Event Description; and f) Identity of any individuals, subjects, or objects/entities associated with the event.
An accurate time source must be established and used consistently across systems to assist with identifying connections between events.
Sensitive information and personally identifiable information contained in security event logs must be limited as much as possible.
Health monitoring must include the detection and response of security event logging process failure. (IE62443

Addition to the above (ref: AU.1.1 & AU.1.2), the following security events must be logged for all firewall & gateway: (ISM/MTM) a) all deny traffic on the devices, b) all permitted traffic through the devices, c) all traffic attempting to leave the devices, d) all system and admin events, e) attempted intrusions, and f) traffic anomalies.

Addition to the above (ref: AU.1.1 & AU.1.2), the following security events must be logged for DNS: (MTM) a) IP or hostname submitting the request, b) name of request, c) type of request, and d) DNS response to request. Note: Verbose DNS logging must be enabled wherever possible to assist in threat hunting and security investigations

Addition to the above (ref: AU.1.1 & AU.1.2), the following security events should be logged for databases: (ISM) a) access or modification of particularly important content, b) queries containing comments, c) queries containing multiple embedded queries, d) database and query alerts or failures, e) database structure changes, f) use of executable commands, and g) database logons and logoffs.

Addition to the above (ref: AU.1.1 & AU.1.2), the following security events should be logged on all web applications: (MTM) a) attempted access that is denied, b) search queries initiated by users, c) user access to a web application, and d) X-Forwarded-For (XFF) request.

Addition to the above (ref: AU.1.1 & AU.1.2), following user security events should be logged (ISO): a) internet activity, b) email activity c) mobile phone activity, d) security breaches, and f) Activity on personal desktop (with approval).
Location information of MTM managed devices should be collected and logged to provide information for investigation when required
Error messages should be generated to provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited (NIST)

Verbose logging should be used wherever system, storage and network constraints allow. (MTM)

specs.text: Systems and platforms must only be chosen from vendors with a commitment to secure-by-design and secure-by-default principles. Vendor must ensure the maintenance of the security of their products. (ISM)
Unneeded accounts, components, services, ports, and functionality (e.g., RDP, Autorun, LanMan, SMB/NetBIOS, LLMNR and WPAD) must either be disabled or removed. (ISM/NIST)

System hardening (including for network devices and cloud resources) must be performed and based on an approved Standard Operating Environment (SOE). SOE must comply with the following: (ISM/ISO/NIST/ACSC) a) must have an owner, b) be consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and standards, c) must be reviewed every 3 years, d) must be validated secure and free from malicious code, and e) must be reviewed by Cyber Security. f) be based on CIS recommendations. In the absence of an SOE, hardening of a system must be based on CIS Level 1 compliance. (Ref: https://downloads.cisecurity.org/)

System must have a logon banner that requires users to acknowledge and accept their security responsibilities before access is granted. Legal advice is sought on the exact wording of logon banners. (ISM)
Unprivileged users are prevented from bypassing, disabling, or modifying security functionality of operating systems or software installed. (ISM)
Unprivileged users are prevented from running elevated script execution engines, such as Windows Script host, PowerShell, and command line. (ISM)

MTM workstations and servers must be protected with: (MTM) a) End Point Protection and Anti-malware solution align with MTM Anti-Malware Standard (A9658). b) Host-Based intrusion detection/prevention systems to identify anomalous behaviour during program execution (e.g., process injection, keystroke logging, driver loading and persistence). (ACSC) c) Mechanisms to restrict incoming network traffic (software-based firewall, NSG, etc.) that is malicious/unauthorised, blocking outgoing network traffic that is not generated by approved/trusted programs, and denying network traffic by default. (ACSC)
All MTM system clocks must be synchronized to MTM authorised time sources. (NIST)
All system implementation and changes impacting security must be approved through MTM’s Change Management process. (MTM)

MTM data must be erased from system when assets are to be released from active service and/or decommissioned. The sanitisation methods must align with MTM Information Asset Secure Handling Guideline (A9443). (NIST/IEC)
The system and software must always be kept up to date with supported versions. (ISO/IEC/NIST)
MTM should only use 64-bit versions of operating systems. (ISM)
The system should have the capability to generate a report listing the currently deployed security settings. (IEC)
The control system shall support supervisor manual override of the current human user authorizations for a configurable time or event sequence. (IEC)
The control system shall support dual approval where an action can result in serious impact on the industrial process. (IEC)
